experiment: Native uncertainty-candidate gates on the same twelve QA examples
selection: Four saved examples per group from the original two-passage pilot, balanced two questions per passage per group; fixed before measuring these candidate gates. All four original made-up cases retained. Natural abstentions exclude the known false-explanation case P2-U2. Identical twelve case IDs and native references to confidence-gate-activation; no selection by the new gate activity.
intervention: None. Fresh greedy generation with no hooks, followed by observation-only token-exact replay. All hooks return None; native MLP and attention remain unchanged.
gate: z=(post_attention_residual-input_mean[layer])/input_std[layer]; raw=z dot e + bias; gate=raw if raw>theta and raw>0 else 0.
timing: A token is coloured by the gate when that token is processed, which can affect the next prediction. Also preserve the final prompt position before the first answer prediction.
dtype: BF16 native model, FP32 gate calculations
metric: Mean over all visible response tokens including zero gates; EOS and other special tokens excluded. Max and active-token counts are separate.
display: Default three priority feature columns; switch to the other four or all seven. Separate question-token and response-token maps, with full-prompt tokens expandable. One colour scale across every measured gate and token.
limitations: Label conditions are hypotheses, not validated confidence signals. Twelve selected QA examples; no interventions or correlation calculation. Two wording controls excluded from QA group means.
query_definition: Tokens whose tokenizer character offsets overlap the exact final user question. Preserve the entire prompt separately; shared instructions and passage are not pooled into query-only means.
